name: Black Mountain-Swannanoa Valley Endowment Fund
next_text: March 1, 2027, 5 PM (every year on March 1, next business day if a weekend)
who: 501(c)(3), government, school and religious organizations (or fiscally sponsored groups) serving Black Mountain and the Swannanoa Valley (Owen School District). One application a year.
funds: Charitable projects that improve quality of life in the valley: programs, equipment, capital. Not scholarships, annual campaigns, debt, festivals or one-time events, or sectarian religious purposes.
contact: Virginia Dollar, Senior Program Officer, dollar@cfwnc.org, 828-367-9907
proof: 18 grants totaling $125,240 in the May 2026 round, including Appalachian Community Relief ($7,500 for its free grocery store).

name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants
next_text: Current round listed as closing Nov 30, 2026 (confirm on walmart.org)
who: 501(c)(3) charities, churches and faith groups with community-benefit projects, schools, government. Needs a Spark Good account and Deed verification first.
funds: Local community projects in the store's service area. The store manager picks.
proof: Three rounds a year. Setup (account plus verification) is the step most groups never finish.

name: Dogwood Health Trust Grants Help Desk
who: Eligible nonprofits and municipalities in Western North Carolina.
funds: Advice and support on grant writing.
proof: Dogwood also runs Community Equity Grants ($50,000 to $350,000 a year) for groups with budgets of $200,000 or more.

name: CFWNC Cultural Resources Grants
next_text: Jan 8, 2027 (this round is for arts councils; categories rotate each round)
who: 501(c)(3) or public agencies in the listed WNC counties, including Buncombe, whose mission fits that round's category.
funds: General operating support for arts and culture groups.
proof: Rounds in January and July, each for one arts category.

name: Pigeon River Fund
by: Community Foundation of Western NC (Duke Energy dam payments)
next_text: About March 15, 2027 (rounds in March and September; confirm)
who: 501(c)(3) and government groups serving Buncombe, Haywood or Madison counties.
funds: Water quality, waterways and wildlife habitat.

name: Duke Energy Foundation, NC themed grants
next_text: Spring rounds (2026 themes closed March 13 and April 30; watch for 2027)
who: 501(c)(3) public charities or government serving Duke Energy communities.
funds: Rotating themes: environmental resilience, storm preparedness, small business support.
proof: $500,000 for 20 environmental resilience grants of $25,000 in 2026.

name: Buncombe County Strategic Partnership Grants
next_text: Next cycle expected to open late 2026 for July 2027 funding (last cycle opened late 2025)
who: Tax-exempt nonprofits incorporated at least 2 years, operating in and serving Buncombe County.
funds: Projects scored on plan, results, capacity, equity and budget.
proof: FY2027 awards were approved in June 2026.

name: Grassroots Arts Program (ArtsAVL / NC Arts Council)
who: 501(c) arts organizations in Buncombe County, operating at least a year.
funds: Arts programs and, for qualified groups, operating costs.

name: CFWNC Human Services and Education Grants
who: 501(c)(3) organizations in the foundation's WNC region.

name: NC Humanities Small Project Grants
next_text: About September 2027 (2026 closed Sept 10; some cycles paused)
who: Nonprofits running public humanities programs: history, culture, storytelling.

name: Food Lion Feeds Charitable Foundation
next_text: Three rounds a year (spring round closed March 13, 2026)
who: Only nonprofits affiliated with Feeding America (for example, MANNA FoodBank partner agencies).
funds: Hunger relief, especially child food insecurity.
proof: Nearly $1 million a round across its region.
